title: Affine etale charts compute quasi-coherent symmetric algebras and ideal quotients
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the small etale site and quasi-coherence of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A module is of finite presentation if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O^{m}\to\mathcal O^{n}$ with $m,n$ finite. For every affine etale chart $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, restriction of a quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ corresponds to the ordinary $R$-module $\mathcal F(U)$ and its associated module sheaf. Restriction followed by sections on $U$ computes kernels, cokernels, images, tensor products and small filtered colimits of quasi-coherent modules. A quasi-coherent module is of finite type (etale locally finitely generated), respectively of finite presentation, if and only if its module of sections has that property on every affine etale chart; either property can instead be tested after restriction to one surjective etale scheme chart. A module of finite presentation is quasi-coherent. There is a quasi-coherent commutative algebra $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ with a linear map $j:\mathcal F\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ such that every linear map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal B$ to an algebra sheaf extends uniquely to an algebra map, and $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F(U))$ canonically. For a map $\psi:\mathcal D\to\mathcal A$ of quasi-coherent commutative algebra sheaves, its kernel ideal and image algebra are quasi-coherent and on $U$ are the ordinary kernel and image of $\psi_U$; the canonical map $\mathcal D/\ker\psi\to\operatorname{Im}\psi$ is an isomorphism. If $e:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ is a map of quasi-coherent modules, its generated ideal $(e(\mathcal E))$, the smallest sheaf of ideals containing the image, and the quotient algebra are quasi-coherent; on $U$ they are the ideal generated by $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$ and the ordinary quotient. This quotient has the universal property for algebra maps killing $e$. Small filtered colimits of quasi-coherent commutative algebras exist in all algebra sheaves, are quasi-coherent, and are computed on every affine etale chart by filtered colimits of $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. An algebra cocone with quasi-coherent vertex is colimiting if its evaluations on all affine etale charts are colimiting.

proof.text:
Fix an affine etale chart $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-cartesian-chart-family], $\mathcal F|_U$ is quasi-coherent on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and the counit and unit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify it canonically with $(\widetilde{\mathcal F(U)})_{\mathrm{et}}$. These identifications respect module maps. They also give, for every module sheaf $H$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, not necessarily quasi-coherent,
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}}((\widetilde M)_{\mathrm{et}},H)=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,H(U))$:
apply the tensor-pullback adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] for $\epsilon:U_{\mathrm{et}}\to U_{\mathrm{Zar}}$, whose direct image is restriction to opens, and then the tilde adjunction. In particular a map with quasi-coherent source on this affine chart is determined by its map of sections, even when its target is arbitrary.

source.place: Tag 03LZ (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent-small-etale); descent.tex Tags 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent) and 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial); schemes.tex Tags 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), 01IA (lemma-quasi-coherent-affine); sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules)

proof.text: Restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the localization pullback of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]. It is exact, and, having a right adjoint by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], preserves all small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Kernels, cokernels, images and small module colimits on $X$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. On $U$, use the exact equivalence [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. In the Zariski affine category the tilde/Gamma unit and counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] give an equivalence with $R$-modules. This equivalence preserves kernels and cokernels, hence images. For an arbitrary small module diagram with colimit $M$, its tilde is the ambient Zariski module colimit by clause (4) of that node; tensor pullback by $\epsilon$ carries it to the ambient etale module colimit. Thus the sections of every one of the displayed constructions on $U$ are the ordinary module construction. This proves the requested filtered-colimit assertion, in fact for all small module colimits.

source.place: Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), proof of (1)--(3); descent.tex Tag 06VE (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits), small etale case

proof.text:
Tensor pullback commutes with tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], both for localization at $U$ and for $\epsilon$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] gives
$(\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal G)|_U\simeq(\widetilde{\mathcal F(U)\otimes_R\mathcal G(U)})_{\mathrm{et}}$.
The local presentations in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] then show that this tensor product is quasi-coherent on $X$: these presentations cover each etale object after an affine open refinement. The displayed formula proves the tensor assertion. For an arrow $W=\operatorname{Spec}R'\to U$ of affine charts, the pullback comparison of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] give the natural scalar-extension formula $\mathcal F(W)=R'\otimes_R\mathcal F(U)$, with restriction $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. This formula will control compatibility of the algebra constructions.

For a quasi-coherent module on an affine chart, [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] identifies etale finite type and finite presentation with their Zariski counterparts; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] identifies these with finite generation and finite presentation of its $R$-module of sections. The two properties are local by their definitions: a finite presentation or finite generating list remains such on a slice, since restriction is exact and preserves coproducts (step 2). If they hold on a surjective etale scheme chart $V\to X$, then by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], for each etale object $W\to X$ the schemes $V\times_XW\to W$ cover $W$; refine them by the etale covers where the required finite presentations or generating lists exist. Composition gives the required local data on $X$. The reverse implication is restriction of those same data. Testing every affine chart is equivalent because every scheme has an affine open cover. Finally any finite-presentation module, without an initial quasi-coherence assumption, already has the local presentations required by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], so is quasi-coherent.

source.place: section-properties-modules, local properties (j),(l) and ensuing items (2)--(4); descent.tex Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties)

proof.text:
For each scheme chart $V\to X$, take the Zariski module corresponding to $\mathcal F|_V$ by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Form its quasi-coherent symmetric algebra using [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] and apply $\epsilon_V^*$. The tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] transports multiplication and the unit to this quasi-coherent etale module $A_V$. On any affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $V$, its sections are $\operatorname{Sym}_B(\mathcal F(W))$. For an arrow $V'\to V$, the affine pullback formula of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections] and [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] identify its pullback with $A_{V'}$: on affines lying over affines the comparison is
$B\otimes_R\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)\simeq\operatorname{Sym}_B(B\otimes_RM)$.
It sends $b\otimes j(m)$ to $b\,j(1\otimes m)$. On overlapping affine opens these maps agree, since they agree on degree-one generators; hence they glue. The same generator formula proves the identity and composition conditions. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-cartesian-chart-family] the $A_V$ therefore give a quasi-coherent module $A$ on $X$. Its multiplication, unit and $j:\mathcal F\to A$ glue by the compatible-map clause of that node, using step 3 for the tensor source. The algebra identities hold after every chart restriction and hence hold globally. This constructs $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)=A$ and its asserted affine evaluations.

source.place: Tag 082A (lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-presentation), symmetric-algebra construction; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LZ; algebra.tex Tag 0C6F (lemma-tensor-algebra-localization), base-change universal-property argument

proof.text: Let $H$ be any commutative algebra sheaf and $a:\mathcal F\to H$ linear. On an affine chart $U$ the ordinary universal property [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] gives the unique algebra map $A(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F(U))\to H(U)$ extending $a_U$. Step 1 extends its underlying linear map uniquely to $A|_U\to H|_U$. This extension preserves multiplication: the two linear maps $A|_U\otimes A|_U\to H|_U$ agree on $U$ by the ring-map equation, and step 3 makes their source quasi-coherent, so step 1 makes them equal. The unit equation follows in the same way with source $\mathcal O_U$. For an affine arrow $W\to U$, the restriction of this extension agrees with the extension on $W$: both have degree-one map $a_W$, and $\mathcal F(W)=\mathcal O(W)\otimes_R\mathcal F(U)$ by step 3. Uniqueness in the ordinary symmetric-algebra universal property and then step 1 identify them. Affine open covers of all etale objects now glue these maps uniquely to $A\to H$; on overlaps use affine open covers again. The sheaf axiom supplies the glued values. Any other algebra extension gives the same maps on every affine chart, hence the same sheaf map. This proves the full universal property, including non-quasi-coherent targets.

source.place: Section 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), symmetric algebra universal property; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LZ, chart construction of step 5

proof.text: For $\psi:\mathcal D\to\mathcal A$, take its kernel and image in module sheaves. They are quasi-coherent and have the asserted affine sections by step 2. The kernel is an ideal since $\psi(dx)=\psi(d)\psi(x)=0$ when $\psi(x)=0$. The image is a unital subalgebra: locally lift two image sections to $\mathcal D$ and apply addition and multiplication there; their sum and product remain locally in the image. The structure map factors through it. Let $K=\ker\psi$ and form the module cokernel $Q=\mathcal D/K$. Its chart sections are $\mathcal D(U)/K(U)$. On these quotients put $\bar d\bar e=\overline{de}$; changing either representative adds an element of the ideal $K(U)$, so this is well-defined and restrictions preserve it. The operations on arbitrary etale objects are obtained by their unique gluing on affine open covers. Thus $Q$ is the algebra quotient. The first-isomorphism map $\bar d\mapsto\psi(d)$ is bijective on every affine chart, since its image is exactly the chart image from step 2. Its inverses commute with restriction by uniqueness, and glue to an inverse sheaf map. This proves $\mathcal D/\ker\psi\simeq\operatorname{Im}\psi$ as algebras.

source.place: Tags 082A and 086Z, kernel ideals and quotient algebras; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (3), with the module and tensor calculations in steps 2--3

proof.text:
Given $e:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, let $I$ be the module image of
$\mathcal D\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$, $d\otimes x\mapsto d\,e(x)$.
Steps 2--3 show $I$ is quasi-coherent and $I(U)$ is the ordinary ideal generated by $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$: its elements are precisely finite sums $\sum d_i e(x_i)$. Multiplication by a section of $\mathcal D$ preserves this image, as is seen on affines from the formula; hence $I$ is an ideal sheaf. It contains $e(\mathcal E)$ by $e(x)=1e(x)$, and every ideal sheaf containing the image of $e$ contains the displayed products, their finite sums, and their local gluings, so contains $I$. This proves minimality. The module cokernel $\mathcal D/I$ is quasi-coherent and has the ordinary quotient on affines by step 2. The quotient operations and their compatibility are the same explicit formulas as in step 7. An algebra map kills $e$ if and only if it kills every $d e(x)$, equivalently $I$. On every affine chart it then factors uniquely through $\mathcal D(U)/I(U)$; the unique factors commute with restriction and glue. Thus the sheaf quotient has the required universal property.

proof.text: For a small filtered diagram of quasi-coherent commutative algebra sheaves $\mathcal A_i$, take the colimit $Q$ of its underlying module sheaves, which exists and is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. Step 2 gives $Q(U)=\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal A_i(U)$ as modules for every affine chart $U$. The ring colimit exists by [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist]; [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module] identifies its underlying module with $Q(U)$. Transport this ring structure to $Q(U)$. For an affine arrow $W\to U$, the compatible algebra maps $\mathcal A_i(U)\to\mathcal A_i(W)\to Q(W)$ induce a ring map $Q(U)\to Q(W)$. It is the existing module restriction because its composites with every module colimit leg agree. This also respects the structure rings. On a nonaffine etale object, restrict its sections to an affine open cover and perform the ring operations there. These results agree on overlaps, checked on affine open covers of the overlaps, so the module-sheaf axiom glues them uniquely. This equips $Q$ with a commutative algebra structure and algebra cocone maps, with precisely the asserted affine algebra colimits.

source.place: Tag 03M1 (2); algebra.tex Section 07N7 (section-colimits), filtered algebra colimits; spaces-limits.tex Tag 082A

proof.text: For any compatible algebra maps $\mathcal A_i\to H$ to an arbitrary algebra sheaf, the ambient module colimit gives a unique linear map $Q\to H$. On each affine chart its map of sections is the ring-colimit factor, because the module and algebra colimits have the same legs (step 9). It therefore preserves the unit and multiplication there. These equations hold on every etale object after an affine open cover, and hence hold by the sheaf axiom. Thus $Q$ is colimiting in all algebra sheaves. More generally let an algebra cocone have quasi-coherent vertex $C$ and colimiting evaluations on all affine etale charts. The just-proved universal property supplies the comparison $Q\to C$. Its affine evaluations are isomorphisms of algebra colimits, with inverse maps commuting with affine restrictions. On any etale object the inverses glue on an affine open cover; uniqueness on overlaps gives a two-sided inverse. Hence $Q\to C$ is an isomorphism and the given cocone is colimiting. This establishes the final chart test without imposing a quasi-coherence condition on the test algebra $H$.
